subject: Avalon Vitals - sustained p95 latency & 502 spikes on private cluster

Subject: sudden p95 latency & 502s since last night

Vivek —

We started seeing a big jump in p95 latency and intermittent 502s on our private VPC cluster starting ~01:00 UTC last night. This is impacting our teletriage API (patient intake) and we had to throttle a few customer flows. We opened an incident on our side and attached a screenshot of the SLO dashboard (avalon_slo_dashboard.png).

Quick details:
- Region: us-west-2 (private deploy)
- Model: quant-v2-13b (pinned)
- Symptoms: sustained p95 from ~180ms -> 620ms, short 502 bursts affecting ~2% of requests between 01:00-04:30 UTC
- Recent change: we toggled the new autoscaling policy last week; nothing else changed on our side overnight

Can Redwood help triage? We need an ETA on fixes and any recommended mitigation steps (fallback model, restart, kernel/quant tuning). This is on the exec radar.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform — Avalon Vitals

Immediate next steps (we'll keep you updated by the hour):
1) Marcus and Dev will pull the node metrics and serving logs to check for kernel mismatch or queued-decoder backpressure.
2) If we see KV-cache pressure, we'll push a parameter tweak to increase prefix cache capacity and reduce aggressive eviction for the affected model.
3) We may propose a temporary fallback to quant-v2-6b (compatible) to buy time while we stabilize the 13b path.
4) If the issue looks like an autoscaler oscillation, suggest a short autoscaler dampening window (5m) or a manual scale-up for the evening traffic window.

Can you confirm whether you enabled any new traffic mirroring or request-level sampling last night? Also, can you share a short time-range of request IDs for a couple of failing requests so our logs team can correlate?

I'll loop back in 30–60m with an initial diagnose.

Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: initial triage notes for Avalon Vitals (RW-3428)

Team — quick notes after first look (logs & node metrics):
- Observed increased kernel preemption and widened GPU SM utilization variance on 3 nodes serving the 13b quant path.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~12% coincident with latency rise; cold prefix misses spike visible around 01:05 UTC.
- A subset of 502s show decoder OOM on worker process then graceful restart; mapped to a spike in batch size aggregation (sustained larger batches during a short burst).
- Autoscaler shows repeated scale-in attempts between 00:45–01:15 UTC; suggested cause: scaling policy too aggressive for short spikes.

Immediate mitigations proposed:
- Increase KV cache size for Avalon cluster by 20% (non-disruptive param push).
- Apply a conservative min-replicas bump to keep steady throughput during the window.
- Patch serving config to cap batch aggregation for the quant-v2-13b variant at a lower threshold (prevent decoder OOM).

I'll prepare the config diff and an operation runbook. If customer agrees to a rolling restart we can clear transient OOMs but prefer param changes first.

-Marcus
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference

I've prepared the config diffs and a small runbook. Changes to apply (non-disruptive):
- Set kv_cache.capacity_bytes += 20%
- Set autoscaler.min_replicas = current + 2 for the affected pool (until 2026-09-18 06:00 UTC)
- Add batch.max_total_tokens = 4096 for quant-v2-13b to cap aggregation

If the above stabilizes metrics in 30–60 minutes we won't need a restart. If we still see OOMs, next step is a rolling restart of the worker pods with a targeted cordon.

I'll push the param changes now and monitor. I'll also upload the redwood_debug_dump_20260916.tar.gz link in 10m.

Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Avalon Vitals - incident update and recommended next steps

Sanjay / Ava — final update from our triage and recommended path forward. Copying execs for visibility.

What we observed:
- Root cause: autoscaler dampening too aggressive + transient batching spike during your ETL window caused larger-than-expected aggregated batches and a KV cache miss storm. Decoder OOMs led to short 502 bursts.
- Impact window: ~2026-09-16T01:00:00Z to 2026-09-16T04:30:00Z. P95 peaked at ~620ms (consistent with your dashboard).

Actions we applied (completed 2026-09-16):
1) Increased KV cache capacity by 20% for the Avalon private pool.
2) Raised min_replicas by +2 and added a 5-minute autoscaler dampening window.
3) Set batch.max_total_tokens=4096 for quant-v2-13b to limit aggregation.
4) Monitored for 12 hours — metrics show p95 returning to baseline and 502 events dropping to <0.1%.

Recommended follow-ups (we propose a joint runbook):
- Schedule a targeted rolling restart tonight during your low-traffic window to clear any lingering worker restarts (optional if you see continued stability).
- We will prepare a permanent autoscaler policy tweak for your production pool (proposal: dampening 5m, conservative scale-in threshold).
- For long-term resilience, consider an automated fallback route to quant-v2-6b for short stabilization windows (we can implement this as a routing policy; requires a short config approval).

If you'd like, we can set a 30-minute postmortem call tomorrow to walk the timeline and approve the policy changes. Thank you for the quick signs and logs — they made correlation much faster.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
